new_statements.quote: アクセントは，「昇り核」（/［/）の有無と位置を語頭から数えた数字で示す。無核型は 0 とする。下北の風間浦村以外は明確な「昇り核」の方言である。 [p. 103] … ちなみに弘前方言の音調は，たとえば連体形言い切りでは，売［ルトキ］］.，［取ル］トキ. などとなる。音調型は方言により，また終止形と連体形でも異なるが，どの方言も / 売ル=/（0 型），/［取ル/（1 型）などで，アクセントは終止形も連体形も同じである。 [p. 104]
new_statements.translation: Accent is shown by the presence or absence and the position of the 'rising kernel' (/[/), as a numeral counted from the beginning of the word; the kernel-less (unaccented) type is 0. Except for Kazamaura village in Shimokita, these are clearly 'rising-kernel' dialects. [p. 103] … Incidentally, the tonal shape of the Hirosaki dialect is, for example in the sentence-final adnominal form, u[rutoki]]., [toru]toki. etc. The tonal shapes differ by dialect and also between conclusive and adnominal forms, but in every dialect it is /uru=/ (type 0), /[toru/ (type 1) etc., and the accent is the same for the conclusive and the adnominal form. [p. 104]

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for tsug1237 has an empty rule field and no existing statements; this paper supplies the type: lexical pitch accent (rising kernel), not stress. Data are from Hirosaki city (two speakers b. 1951/1952) and Goshogawara city (b. 1950), both former Tsugaru domain.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tsugaru (Hirosaki, Goshogawara) is a lexical pitch accent system of the 'rising-kernel' (noboriкaku) type: each word either has no kernel (type 0) or has a kernel whose position (counted in moras from the word start) is lexically specified; the kernel is realized as a pitch rise at that mora, with a following fall whose placement depends on the dialect and the syntactic form. No word stress is described; prominence is pitch, not stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed (none in a pitch accent system).
new_statements.exceptions: Kazamaura (Shimokita, a Nambu-han site, not Tsugaru) is a 'one-place prominence' type rather than a rising-kernel type (p. 103); the phonetic tone shape of the same kernel differs between Iwate and Hirosaki/Tsugaru (p. 104).
new_statements.identity_note: Hirayama & Sato 2003 covers Aomori Prefecture as a whole (Tsugaru and Nambu dialects). The Uwano data explicitly labelled Tsugaru-han come from Hirosaki city and Goshogawara city (2019) and Aomori city and Tsugaru city/former Shariki village (2020); Hachinohe, Kazamaura (Shimokita), Morioka and Shizukuishi in the same papers are Nambu dialect (Iwate or former Nambu domain), not Tsugaru, and Kazamaura is a different ('one-place prominence') accent type.

new_statements.quote: 全体として見ると，外来語のアクセント体系も，和語と同様，モーラ数より 1 つ多い Pn=n+1 の対立を基本とする。ただし同時に，2 モーラ語以下では無核型がなく，6 モーラ語（以上）では語頭核が極くわずかとなり，モーラ数を問わず語末核も少数派である，という制限がある。 [pp. 62-63] … ⓪：/ ○○○ =/：○○○（低平調）（岩手），○○[○（青森）。「=」は無核型の印。 ①：/[○○○ /：[○]○○ .，[○○○…（岩手）；[○○]○ .，[○○○]…（津軽） [p. 49] … These dialects exhibit n+1 contrastive pitch patterns for n-mora foreign words (3≦n≦6), with these patterns varying in accordance with the weakness of the mora structure. [English abstract, p. 69]
new_statements.translation: Seen as a whole, the accent system of foreign words too, like that of native words, is based on a Pn = n+1 contrast, one more than the number of moras. At the same time there are restrictions: words of two moras or fewer have no kernel-less type, in words of six moras (or more) word-initial kernels become extremely few, and word-final kernels are a minority whatever the mora count. [pp. 62-63] … Type 0: /○○○=/: ○○○ (low level) (Iwate), ○○[○ (Aomori); '=' marks the kernel-less type. Type 1: /[○○○/: [○]○○. , [○○○… (Iwate); [○○]○. , [○○○]… (Tsugaru). [p. 49]

new_statements.relation_note: Same conclusion as Uwano 2019: lexical pitch accent with n+1 contrast. Tsugaru data here are from Aomori city (older data, speaker b. 1935) and Tsugaru city (former Shariki village, b. 1947); the other sites (Morioka, Shizukuishi, Kazamaura) are Nambu dialect, not Tsugaru.
new_statements.rule_in_words: An n-mora word has n+1 possible contrastive pitch patterns (kernel on any mora, or no kernel); the kernel position is lexical but partly predictable from mora structure ('weak' moras — special moras and narrow-vowel moras — avoid bearing the kernel, so the kernel tends to fall on the nearest 'non-weak' mora). Prominence is a pitch rise at the kernel mora; there is no word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: No kernel-less type in words of 1-2 moras; initial kernel very rare in 6+ mora words; final-kernel type a minority; Aomori-side (Tsugaru) forms are always accented (kerneled) and place the kernel further forward than the Iwate side in several items (pp. 62-63, 'chiikisa' section).
new_statements.identity_note: Hirayama & Sato 2003 covers Aomori Prefecture as a whole (Tsugaru and Nambu dialects). The Uwano data explicitly labelled Tsugaru-han come from Hirosaki city and Goshogawara city (2019) and Aomori city and Tsugaru city/former Shariki village (2020); Hachinohe, Kazamaura (Shimokita), Morioka and Shizukuishi in the same papers are Nambu dialect (Iwate or former Nambu domain), not Tsugaru, and Kazamaura is a different ('one-place prominence') accent type.
